articles.title: LeBron's Fanatics Deal Includes Helicopter Use
articles.summary: The helicopter has repeatedly gone between NYC and Philly.
articles.body:
LeBron James isn't paying a dime for his commute to and from Philadelphia to play for the Sixers.

A Fanatics source told Front Office Sports that James has been using the company's aviation as part of his broader deal with the company. James signed a multiyear trading card partnership with Fanatics in January 2024, while he agreed to a deal with the Sixers in July and will reportedly live in New York City while playing for the team.

He has been seen taking a helicopter with multiple Fanatics logos to and from Philadelphia.

"The deal we signed with Fanatics almost three years ago includes access to their corporate aviation," a spokesperson for James told FOS . "It's a feature in many of their deals with their largest athletes and we appreciate their partnership as LeBron splits his time between New York and Philadelphia."

A one-way chopper from New York City to Philadelphia is about $4,000 to $10,000 . It's not known how much Fanatics's deal with James is worth.

Flight records show the Fanatics helicopter James has used made a dozen round-trips between Philadelphia and New York in the past week. A one-way trip normally takes about 30 minutes, cutting what is normally about a 90-minute to two-hour drive.

James, who has made nearly $600 million in his 24-year NBA career, signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Sixers in July. He will earn a career-low $3.87 million this season.

But he's making it back through several endorsement deals, including with Fanatics and a recent deal with Polymarket that FOS reported last month is worth about $15 million annually.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | 'Fear may never completely go away': Sujeet Kalkal on turning Olympic heartbreak into Asian Games gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Two years ago, Sujeet Kalkal was stranded at Dubai International Airport, watching his Olympic dream slip away with every passing hour.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two years ago, Sujeet Kalkal was stranded at Dubai International Airport, watching his Olympic dream slip away with every passing hour.On his way to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the Asian Olympic Qualifying Tournament, Kalkal was stuck in Dubai for three days after floods disrupted his travel plans. By the time a flight was arranged, it was too late. He could not reach Bishkek in time, and with it went his chance to qualify for the Paris Olympics.Two years later, the disappointment of Dubai has been replaced by an Asian Games gold. Kalkal, the world No. 2 in the men's 65kg category, fought back from 2-9 down against Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev in the final to win 10-9, ending India's eight-year wait for a wrestling gold at the Games.The comeback was symbolic of what Kalkal's career has looked like since that Olympic setback. He has had to rebuild, compete through the disappointment and find a way back to the biggest stages. On Sunday, he did that with an Asian Games title.When the final whistle came, Kalkal folded his hands, looked up and thanked God. He then took a lap of the arena with the Indian tricolour draped around his shoulders, tears and a broad smile.For a wrestler who had once been denied even the chance to fight for an Olympic place, the moment carried a little more weight than an Asian Games gold."This gold means a lot to me. Not just because it is an Asian Games gold, but because there is so much behind this medal. The last few years have had many ups and downs, and I missed a few opportunities, but I never lost belief in myself," Kalkal told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview on his way back to Imlota village in Bhiwani, Haryana, where his parents were waiting to welcome him.The Dubai episode, he says, is now behind him. What remains is the lesson from it - and a much bigger target."Paris was very difficult for me to miss, but that experience made me stronger instead of breaking me. LA 2028 is obviously a very big goal for me," Kalkal said.And he is clear about what he wants from that opportunity. "Olympics mein jaana hai toh sirf participate karne ke liye nahi jaana, bhaisaab. Gold ke liye jaana hai [“If you’re going to the Olympics, don’t go just to participate, brother. Go there to win gold]."India had not won a wrestling gold at the Asian Games since 2018. Kalkal's victory ended that wait and added another major title to a career that already includes an U23 World Championship crown, Asian Championships success and a Zagreb Open triumph."India has won a wrestling gold at the Asian Games after eight years, so being a part of it is very special for me. This medal reminds me that if you keep working hard, your time will come," he said.The road to the Asian Games gold was not easy for Kalkal. He had a challenging draw, but handled each bout with confidence.After a comfortable opening victory, he made a statement in the quarterfinals by throwing Iran's Abbas Ebrahimzadehsavadkouhi from a standing position within the opening 20 seconds.The semifinal brought an even bigger test, but Kalkal overcame Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka to reach the gold medal bout.Then came the final against Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev, and it looked like the toughest challenge of them all.Instead of allowing the deficit to affect him, Kalkal fought his way back into the contest. He produced eight points to turn a seven-point deficit into a 10-9 victory and seal the Asian Games title."The simple plan was to wrestle my own way and not be impressed by my opponent's name. Whether he is an Olympic champion, a world champion or anyone else, everyone starts from zero on the mat. I just trusted my preparation and my strength. I knew that if I executed my best, I could beat anyone. Instead of thinking too much during the match, I just had to fight for every single point," he said.Kalkal also dedicated the gold to the country and remembered his father, who stood by him throughout his journey."I dedicate this gold to the whole of India. Of course, my first call was to my father. He has supported me tremendously throughout this journey, and without his support, it would have been impossible for me to reach this point. His support will always remain with me," the Indian wrestler said.The final also reflected the mental change Kalkal says came from the disappointment of 2024."Fear may never completely go away, but now I know how to fight with fear. When you go through tough situations in life, small things stop bothering you. What happened in Dubai, missing the Olympic qualifiers - every experience taught me something," the Indian wrestler said."Now I don't run away from pressure. I enjoy pressure because those are the moments when you realise how strong you actually are," Kalkal said.The Asian Games gold now joins an already impressive list of achievements for Kalkal, but he is not dwelling on the medals he has already won. The next target is Los Angeles. And this time, he wants to get there on his own terms."Gold ke liye jaana hai."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Other side of India's Asian Games success: 201 athletes won just 6 bronze, 137 returned empty-handed
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s 85-medal haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games was its secondbest finish, but the headline numbers don’t reveal everything.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s 85-medal haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games was its secondbest finish, but the headline numbers don’t reveal everything.A sport-by-sport audit by TOI shows that 137 Indian athletes across 16 disciplines returned empty-handed, exposing persistent gaps in the country’s medal ambitions.India’s pruned-down 495-member contingent competed across 36 sport disciplines and finished fourth with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.Yet 137 athletes across 16 disciplines won nothing.Another 64 athletes across six sports managed six bronze — one each in kurash, mixed martial arts, rowing, sepaktakraw, soft tennis and wushu. The zero-medal list included canoeing (19 athletes), cycling (14), equestrian (7), esports (15), fencing (20), gymnastics (1), judo (3), karate (2), rugby sevens (13), sport climbing (2), surfing (4), swimming (12), taekwondo (3), tennis (7), teqball (3) and volleyball (12). The six-bronze group comprised kurash (6 athletes), MMA (2), rowing (22), sepaktakraw (21), soft tennis (6) and wushu (7).In all, 201 athletes accounted for just six bronze medals across the 22 disciplines mentioned above. In other prominent sports with sizable athlete numbers, table tennis sent 10 athletes and returned with one bronze and badminton’s 20-member contingent managed one bronze in the men’s team event. Together, the two sent 37 athletes and produced only two bronze.India contested in 259 medal events in AichiNagoya and won medals in just 20, a 7.7% eventpodium conversion rate. Of 356 medals available in which India featured, the nation collected 85, a conversion rate of only 23.9%.The spending breakdownThe govt spent Rs 259.69 crore on 19 sports as part of the overall total expenditure during the current Asian Games cycle (Nov 2023-Aug 2026), led by badminton (Rs 49.26 cr), cycling track (Rs 35.9 cr), fencing (Rs 28.2 cr), table tennis (Rs 25.3 cr), tennis (Rs 22.4 cr) and canoe/kayak (Rs 20.1 cr). Other allocations included rowing (Rs 13.8 cr,) swimming (Rs 10.8 cr), gymnastics (Rs 10.49 cr), judo (Rs 8.05 cr), wushu (Rs 7.8 cr), volleyball (Rs 6.5 cr), sepaktakraw (Rs 5.7 cr), equestrian (Rs 3.7 cr), rugby (Rs 3.63 cr), surfing (Rs 2.9 cr), karate (Rs 1.99 cr), soft tennis (Rs 1.6 cr) and kurash (Rs 1.6 cr).On three sports – MMA, eSports and sport climbing, the govt spent no money. As per the govt’s own estimates, it spent approximately Rs 703 cr across 30 disciplines during the Nov 2023-Aug 2026 preparation cycle. The Rs 703 cr included about Rs 118 cr for domestic training and national coaching camps, Rs 40 cr for overseas training, Rs 252 cr for international competition exposure, Rs 89 cr for equipment, Rs 86 cr for foreign coaches/support staff and Rs 118 cr for other expenses, including Indian experts, championships, competitions in India, grassroots and coach development.Also, a total of 427 athletes who were part of the govt’s various programmes and schemes participated in the Games, including 77 athletes from Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) Core group, 78 from TOPS Development 78, 48 from Target Asian Games Group (TAGG), 65 Khelo India Athlete (KIA), 25 from National Centre of Excellence (NCoE) and 134 from National Coaching Camps (NCCs).The Glasgow comparison is revealing, though not like-for-like. India had 122 athletes and para-athletes in 10 sports at the curtailed 2026 Commonwealth Games and won 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze — also finishing fourth. The Asian Games contingent was 4.06 times larger, but its 85-medal haul was only 2.18 times Glasgow’s. Medal efficiency was 17.2 per 100 athletes in Aichi-Nagoya against 32 in Glasgow.The message is that at this level, the medal base remains concentrated.For a country investing Rs 703 cr across a multi-year cycle, the next challenge is clear: turn wider participation, exposure and support into wider podium conversion.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In Japan, women’s sumo battles tradition and a male-dominated system for survival
articles.summary: KYOTO: It’s a rainy Sunday morning but that hasn’t stopped more than 100 women and girls from making their way to the Kyoto City Budo Centre, Japan’s
articles.body: KYOTO: It’s a rainy Sunday morning but that hasn’t stopped more than 100 women and girls from making their way to the Kyoto City Budo Centre, Japan’s oldest martial arts performance hall. Built in 1899, the original structure is mostly out of bounds for visitors. But a recently built adjoining hall is buzzing with activity.The women are dressed in wrestling singlets, wearing the traditional mawashi, the thick belt associated with sumo, over it. At the centre of the hall is a ring that looks like a dohyo, the raised platform on which sumo is contested. It looks like one. But it isn’t.Women are traditionally barred from stepping into a sumo dohyo, a practice rooted in religious beliefs that have long associated menstruation with impurity. Yet, inside this hall, women are doing precisely what tradition has told them they cannot: sumo wrestling.More than 600 women in over 70 clubs practise the traditional form of wrestling in Japan, despite the resistance it has faced. In the wrestling venue at the Asian Games, when a senior official of the Japan Wrestling Association was asked about women’s sumo, he laughed before dismissing it: “It’s no sport for women.”But it wasn’t always this way. Historical research suggests women participated in sumo as far back as the fifth century. The sport also had periods of popularity between 1603 and 1868 and in the early 20th century, before women’s sumo was banned in 1926 on moral and traditional grounds.It returned in organised form in 1997. Yet, amateur women’s sumo continues to fight for survival. The Japan Sumo Association does not recognise it, leaving private clubs, schools and universities to keep it alive.At universities and a few clubs, women train alongside their male counterparts. Even the arrival of Japan’s first female prime minister has not changed the equation. Sanae Takaichi, who became prime minister last year, had said, “I respect tradition. I will not step on the dohyo.”There are, however, women like Airi Hisano, considered the strongest woman sumo wrestler of the country, trying to change things. The 27-yearold Tokyo native began with karate and judo before finding her calling in sumo at Nihon University.She was fortunate to find support at home. “My family wants me to do my best,” she said.It wasn’t easy. “Of course people made fun of me because, in rigid gender spaces, acceptance wasn’t easy. But that didn’t bother me. Also, it wasn’t an Olympic sport,” said Airi, who works in the administrative section of Tachihi Holdings.A heavyweight competitor, Airi balances training with her day job, where she also doubles as a security guard. She holds a third-degree black belt in judo and a first-degree black belt in karate. “We still have a long way to go,” she said.Not far from where Airi was preparing for her bout, Katsumasa Kawase was putting three girls from Team Shiga through their warm-up. “Being a sumo wrestler myself, I didn’t want my daughters to be denied the opportunity when they wanted to try it,” Kawase said, helping his daughters Momoka and Yuzuki warm up.The physical demands are no different from those faced by their male counterparts. The typical diet includes chicken or pork, vegetables, rice and candied sweet potatoes. But muscle is not the biggest hurdle. Awareness is.Morita, who handles public relations for Yoko Sumo Club, an all-women’s team based in Tokyo, said the club was formed in 2024 and has remained exclusively female. “A major challenge is that many people are still unfamiliar with women’s sumo,” she said.What keeps the wrestlers going? “They continue believing that the sport will eventually be included in the Olympics,” Morita said.Women coaches are still few. One of them is Mao Ueda of Hirakata Sumo Club. A former judoka and jiu-jitsu practitioner, she took up coaching after seeing an opportunity to combine her experience in martial arts with the nuances of sumo.“It’s a long road,” she said. The biggest challenge, she believes, comes after university. “With no recognition, money or future, most girls drop out after university. We need a structure to change that,” Ueda said.However, Momoka, 9, knows little about any of that. Two years into the sport, she knows only that she wants to become an Olympian.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WWE RAW Results & Highlights 5-October-2026: Roman Reigns brings back Solo Sikoa to reunite with The Bloodline, chaotic No.1 contender's match, and more
articles.summary: WWE RAW aired its October 5 episode from the Enterprise Center in St. Louis, Missouri.
articles.body: WWE RAW aired its October 5 episode from the Enterprise Center in St. Louis, Missouri. This was the go-home show for their upcoming Premium Live Event, Money in the Bank 2026. Roman Reigns returned to handle family business while continuing his feud with LA Knight heading into the WWE PLE. He also brought back Solo Sikoa to team up with The Usos for a match against 946.Plus, other exciting matches took place, and a chaotic main event concluded with a new match made official for Money in the Bank.What happened in the opening segment of WWE RAW in St.Louis?LA Knight opened the show just as Roman Reigns arrived in the building. The Megastar spoke about the Bloodline and 946. He then began berating Reigns, leading to the OTC’s entrance. Both men had a heated verbal exchange, and Knight concluded the promo by saying that he would walk out of Money in the Bank as the new World Champion.Bron Breakker & Austin Theory vs. Penta & Je’Von EvansThis was the first match of the night featuring The Vision against Penta and Je’Von Evans in a tag showdown. The Vision attacked Penta as he was making his entrance. The action went back and forth between both teams. In the final moments, Maxxine Dupri distracted the referee, and Logan Paul slid the brass knuckles in the ring. However, instead of Austin Theory, Je’Von Evans grabbed them, knocked him out, and pinned Theory for the victory. Bronson Reed ambushed him and Penta, but Oba Femi came out to their aid.Sol Ruca & Lola Vice vs. Raquel Rodriguez & Roxanne PerezThis was the second tag team match of the night. Both teams held up their own against each other. Toward the end of the bout, Lola Vice accidentally took out her own partner, Sol Ruca, allowing Roxanne Perez to capitalize and score the victory for her team.Ethan Page vs. Rey FenixThe match saw Rey Fenix defend his AAA World Cruiserweight Championship against Ethan Page. Both superstars delivered an instant-classic title bout that kept the audience glued to their seats. In the final moments, Fenix went for the Mexican Muscle Buster, but Page countered it. This led Fenix to utilize the small package and claim the pinfall to win the match.Rey Mysterio & Dragon Lee vs. Dominik Mysterio & JD McDonaghThe tag team bout between both sides was fast-paced bout. It concluded with Big Cass interfering and JD McDonagh using a major headbutt to seal the victory for his team.Becky Lynch vs. Liv MorganThe main event featured Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch clashing in a No.1 contender’s match. It was a highly intense bout with both women fighting for a title shot at Money in the Bank. In the final moments, Stephanie Vaquer came out to the ringside area, but found herself assaulted by both Lynch and Morgan. This agitated her to the point that she attacked them both. She then demanded to defend her WWE Women’s World title against both of them for Money in the Bank and Adam Pearce made it official.Also read: What does Naomi’s rumored WWE return mean for The Bloodline and its battle with The 946Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Major triple-threat title match set for WWE Money in the Bank 2026
articles.summary: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Premium Live Event is just days away, and a huge showdown has been made official.
articles.body: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Premium Live Event is just days away, and a huge showdown has been made official. It will feature three competitors from the women's division battling it out in a high-stakes match, and only one will leave as the new champion.WWE Money in the Bank 2026 will feature a major Women's title matchThe October 5 episode of Monday Night RAW featured a blockbuster main event match between Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan. The match was to determine the No.1 contender to Stephanie Vaquer's WWE Women's World Championship at Money in the Bank 2026. This came off the heels of a feud brewing between the three women ever since Vaquer and Lynch returned to WWE on RAW after SummerSlam, after their respective hiatuses.The match was nothing short of heated, with tensions between Morgan and Lynch, who are longtime rivals themselves. Both women came hitting with their best moves from their respective arsenals. Yet neither was ready to give up that easily, with a huge title opportunity at stake. Overall, it was a highly exhilarating bout worthy of the main event of Monday Night RAW. However, the interesting turn came towards the end of the bout.Stephanie Vaquer came out to neutralize the threat of Morgan's allies, the Judgment Day, and then stood on the apron. This saw Becky Lynch accidentally take out Vaquer. Following that, Morgan attacked Vaquer and then turned her focus on Lynch. As they continued to trade blows, La Primera came back in the ring and attacked them both at the same time, ending the match in a double DQ. She then inflicted a major beatdown on both competitors, leading to the arrival of RAW GM Adam Pearce to control the situation.In a surprising turn of events, Vaquer demanded to face both Morgan and Lynch with her Women's World title on the line. The crowd came unglued, and Pearce made it official for Money in the Bank 2026. While it is commendable for Stephanie Vaquer to take on a tough challenge for her title, her chances of retaining it are slim now. So we will have to wait and see whether she can walk out of Money in the Bank with the gold still strapped around her waist.Also read: What does Naomi’s rumored WWE return mean for The Bloodline and its battle with The 946Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luka Doncic scores 21 as Lakers unveil new defense in preseason win over Kings
articles.summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic puts on a show with Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves sidelined by injury in a 127-103 preseason win over the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
The Lakers pressed, switched and swarmed from the opening whistle. After the Sacramento Kings were caught for a shot-clock violation on the first possession of Monday's preseason game, Luka Doncic raised his fists toward the Lakers bench with a triumphant grin to symbolize the successful start.

But Doncic's smile toward his teammates had a hint of sarcasm; this is still just an exhibition.

The Lakers teased their new defensive identity in a 127-103 preseason win against the Sacramento Kings on Monday at Golden 1 Center, rolling out their deep group of wings to overcome a short-handed bench.

Playing without star center Walker Kessler , who missed the game with a finger injury, and guard Austin Reaves (ankle), Doncic led the Lakers with 21 points. He took a hard knee to the side of his quad midway through the second quarter, but stayed in the game. With the Lakers up 26 points at halftime, Doncic didn't need to return.

"We all had fun out there," said Doncic, who relished the chance to play in his first competitive basketball game in six months, one of the longest breaks of his career. "Especially with Matisse [Thybulle] and Ziaire [Williams], just that beginning of the game, the start, that's contagious for everybody, and how they start the game, it was inspirational."

The star guard actually was bringing down the team's shooting average. While he was three-for-nine from three-point range in the first half, his teammates combined to make nine of their first 13 three-pointers. Williams led with perfect three-for-three shooting from distance with 13 points and one steal while serving as the Lakers' top on-ball defender. Thybulle, another key defensive offseason addition, had two steals and made two threes.

At halftime, coaches showed players a clip of Williams, a 6-foot-9 forward who signed on a minimum contract, guarding the ball full court. The highlight then showed how Doncic's energy picked up. Thybulle followed suit.

"You don't wanna be the only guy out there that's not being physical, not picking up full, not being a pest," Williams said. "Coming in, I knew that I saw that the team could use that, someone who could pick up full and could guard the main ball handler and really set the tone on that end. I try to just focus on that every possession."

Coach JJ Redick, in his third season with the Lakers, said it was the first time in his tenure that he felt the team had multiple players who were capable of handling that defensive responsibility. The Lakers call it their "line of confrontation." Williams, Thybulle, second-year forward Adou Thiero and guard Quentin Grimes were among the players who guarded the ball full court. The Lakers forced four steals in the first quarter and 15 for the game. They averaged 8.5 per game last season.

The product Monday is far from what the Lakers hope to show in their regular-season opener Oct. 21 against the Golden State Warriors.

Kessler was wearing a splint on his left pinky finger after he jammed it on the backboard during practice last week. Redick doesn't expect any of the injuries that kept Reaves, guard Collin Sexton (lower body) and two-way forward Arthur Kaluma (lower body) to be long-term.

Reaves, who tweaked his ankle in practice, still went through his pregame warmup routine Monday.

Even without two of their three top players, the Lakers overwhelmed the Kings, who are expected to be among the worst teams in the Western Conference again. Rookie point guard Darius Acuff, the No. 7 pick in last April's draft, had 19 points with four assists and five turnovers.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Calha is ready 💪, Amorim woes and Spalletti's XI: morning news☀️
articles.summary: Last night's fine win over Turkey brings the international break for Italy and the other national teams to a close, after domestic leagues were put on hold....
articles.body:
Last night's fine win over Turkey brings the international break for Italy and the other national teams to a close, after domestic leagues were put on hold. Serie A returns on Saturday.

The top clubs will therefore be back in action very soon. Let's take a look at this morning's biggest stories.

Juventus want to get their push for the top spots back on track straight away and are not underestimating their trip to Cagliari , currently fourth in the table. After a three-week break, Spalletti is expected to rely on his regular starters and the players who stayed at Continassa, including Bremer, McKennie and Kolo Muani. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the aim is to avoid another slip-up in Sardinia and make the best possible start to a busy October, with seven matches in around twenty days across the league and Europa League.

In defence, Spalletti will build around Bremer , alongside Kalulu and Lucumí, while McKennie is expected to return to the starting line-up. Up front, Kolo Muani is set to keep his place, still searching for his first Serie A goal of 2026, with Conceiçao favoured over Zhegrova after returning from international duty with Portugal. The Kosovan, who scored a goal and provided an assist for his national team, is nevertheless an important option off the bench. Juve want to start strongly: after beating Atalanta, the Bianconeri are three points off the top.

🚑 Milan, injuries force a reshuffle for the Rossoneri

Milan have lost two important players on the flanks. Their first serious injury setback of the season concerns Alexis Saelemaekers , who will need surgery on his right ankle and could be out for at least four months. Further complicating Ruben Amorim 's plans is the injury to Pervis Estupinan , who suffered a knee problem while playing for Ecuador. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the coach will therefore have to rethink both flanks, starting with the match against Sassuolo .

On the left, the most natural solution is Bartesaghi , while Amorim could turn to the in-form Diego Moreira to replace Saelemaekers, or consider more cautious alternatives such as playing Rabiot out wide or returning to a 3-4-2-1. The Belgian had become an important part of the Rossoneri's new system, and his absence will force the coach to find a different balance just as a run of seven matches in twenty days begins.

Inter's playmaking duties are returning to Hakan Calhanoglu . The Turkish midfielder has trained with the squad for the first time since his latest adductor problem and is now aiming to be available for the match against Parma . According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Chivu will have a week to assess his fitness and decide how much to use him in the league and Champions League.

His recovery also comes at a delicate time for the player's future, with his contract expiring in June 2027 . His performances and, above all, his ability to stay fit will also be crucial to any renewal, with Inter needing to assess the terms of a potential new deal. In the meantime, Zielinski remains the main alternative in the playmaker role and has already deputised for Calhanoglu in recent matches. Now, however, the Turk wants to put his injury problems behind him and reclaim his place at the heart of Inter's midfield.

Aurelio De Laurentiis has returned to Castel Volturno to take stock of Napoli 's current situation, with particular attention to their injured players. The president met with Massimiliano Allegri and sporting director Giovanni Manna, while according to CalcioNapoli24 , one of the priorities is to gain a better understanding of the injury problems that have been affecting the team for several weeks.

Saturday's match against Frosinone is also a key focus, seen as crucial to getting the Azzurri back on track after a difficult start. De Laurentiis wants answers and greater consistency, while Allegri's staff await the return of several players: Meret, Spinazzola and Marianucci are close to rejoining the squad, while McTominay and Anguissa's fitness still needs to be assessed.

Roma have returned to training at Trigoria ahead of their trip to Como, the first fixture in a long, gruelling run. The main doubt concerns Bryan Cristante , who is dealing with inflammation of a collateral knee ligament. "He's receiving treatment; it takes time," Gasperini told Sky Sport , suggesting that no risks will be taken, with the match against Real Madrid also on the horizon.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Cristante is therefore expected to start on the bench at Como, with de Roon ready to make his first start in a Roma shirt. The Dutchman is expected to partner Koné in midfield, in a match with special significance for the former Atalanta player, who will immediately be reunited with familiar surroundings. For Gasperini, meanwhile, it will mark the start of a run of nine matches in 27 days .

Lazio continue to monitor their injury list ahead of the league's return. Cancellieri , who has been dealing with a cut to his knee that required stitches, is aiming to rejoin the squad, and there is optimism over his availability for the match against Monza . Dele-Bashiru and Marusic , both on the road to recovery, have the same target. According to Corriere dello Sport , Rovella , sidelined since 30 August with a calf injury, will also try to speed up his return.

The timeline is less certain for Cataldi , who is dealing with quadriceps fatigue: the midfielder could target the match against Juventus on 18 October, but there are no guarantees. Gudmundsson , however, will be unavailable, still sidelined after dislocating his right shoulder. Lazio therefore hope to recover at least some of their absent players for their next league fixture.

🤑 Fiorentina must sell before moving for Tiago Gabriel

Tiago Gabriel is one of the names linked with Fiorentina ahead of the January transfer window. The Lecce defender has attracted interest from several clubs, including Sporting Lisbon , and is valued at close to €30 million . According to La Nazione , a fee of that size would make an immediate signing difficult, but Fabio Paratici could work with agent Jorge Mendes on a deal structure that would defer part of the payment.

The move would, however, depend on the future of Marin Pongracic . Before making a serious move for the Lecce centre-back, Fiorentina would first need to find a new club for the Croatian and bring in a substantial fee from his sale. Only then would the Viola have the financial room to try to bring Tiago Gabriel to Florence.

articles.title: Watch Luka Doncic moment in Los Angeles Lakers game which could be a major concern
articles.summary: Luka Doncic looked like he was on another level in the first half against the Sacramento Kings, but one moment towards the end will lead to fans worrying. Th...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic looked like he was on another level in the first half against the Sacramento Kings, but one moment towards the end will lead to fans worrying.

The Los Angeles Lakers destroyed the Sacramento Kings 127-100 in their preseason clash. Luka Doncic led the way, scoring 21 points in 16 first-half minutes. His performance included back-to-back three pointers, and gave fans plenty of reasons to be excited.

It is a big season for Doncic. He is officially the main man in LA after LeBron James' departure, and he needs to live up to that responsibility. While his actual play showed that he is ready, there was a moment in the clash which showed that his body might not be.

Luka Doncic was seen limping on the court in the final minutes of the first half

The Slovenian superstar was done for the evening at the half. The Lakers essentially emptied their bench for the second part of the game. Leaving Doncic in for longer would have almost seemed unfair to the Kings. He was helping the Lakers casually run up the score in the second quarter.

While the takeaways from his performance were all largely positive, there was one hiccup right at the end. In recent years, Luka has become a bit injury-prone. As the first half came to an end, he was spotted limping quite heavily, which is certainly concerning for fans of the team.

Luka is now in his prime on arguably the NBA's biggest franchise. The clock is ticking for him to get some major accolades before people start losing faith in his ability to maximise his generational talent. Health is the only thing which is likely to stop him, making this a problem.

Doncic has hobbled on the court various times in the past. Anyone who watches him knows that Luka often looks banged up when he plays. Lakers fans will certainly be hoping it was just a painful hit and nothing more. If he does get injured for whatever reason, it will be the end of the Lakers' aspirations this year.

articles.title: Saints legend Steve Gleason hits Peyton Manning with savage ‘forehead’ joke
articles.summary: Monday Night Football brought out the stars in New Orleans as the Saints suffered an ugly 45-24 loss. Franchise legend Alvin Kamara looked like his vintage...
articles.body:
Monday Night Football brought out the stars in New Orleans as the Saints suffered an ugly 45-24 loss . Franchise legend Alvin Kamara looked like his vintage self but left with a knee injury on a night when legendary former Saints special teams hero Steve Gleason watched alongside Peyton and Eli Manning.

Gleason, who has a statue outside of the Caesars Superdome, had jokes for the legendary NFL brothers including one on the enormous size of Peyton Manning 's forehead.

"Steve, how easy would it have been to block Peyton as a punter?" Eli Manning asked the former Saints punt blocker extraordinaire alongside football of his brother Peyton Manning attempting to coffin corner punt.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Peyton, unfortunately for both of us, long before I'd hit the ball, I'd hit your forehead," Gleason said, drawing laughter from the Manning duo.

Gleason blocked a punt in September 2006 against the Falcons in the Louisiana Superdome's 'Rebirth Game,' its first since Hurricane Katrina struck the area. Gleason got a statue for his efforts as the play became a symbol of hope and rebirth for a city that was put through hell during the Category 3-5 hurricane. Manning is the son of Saints legend Archie Manning who has been known to take jokes about his appearance in stride.

The Saints Monday Night football loss caused coach Kellen Moore's team to drop to 1-3 while fans breathed a sigh of relief over news on Chris Olave's injury scare . Kamara had a night that was frustrating but also special as he thrilled fans with his pair of TD scores.

Gleason didn't get to watch the Saints get a much needed win, but he did have fun calling the game with two legendary former players. The Saints have a long way to go to match the Manning brothers' feats during their playing days, but will have another opportunity to move forward in their October 11 game at Minnesota.

articles.title: Los Angeles Dodgers Manager Drops Honest Andy Pages Quote Amid Braves Series
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts dropped an honest Andy Pages quote amid the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves. The post Los Angeles Dodgers Manager Dr...
articles.body:
The National League Division Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves is tied 1-1.

The Dodgers won the first game of the series 5-3 on Saturday. The Braves won the second game 3-2 on Sunday.

Game 3 of the Series is scheduled to start at 3:00 p.m. PDT on Tuesday at Truist Park.

Ahead of Game 3, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts dropped an honest quote involving struggling outfielder Andy Pages.

Los Angeles Dodgers' Dave Roberts Makes Honest Andy Pages Statement Amid Atlanta Braves Series

Dave Roberts said Andy Pages is "trying to do too much" at the plate. Still, even in the backdrop of his struggles last postseason, don't expect that to lead to taking Pages out of the lineup just yet.

DAVE ROBERTS: Yeah, this is one of those things that I'm gonna continue to give Andy leash. I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we're gonna need him to be an active part of our team.

And so I hope it doesn't get to that point. We're not there yet.

I think that this is, for me, given to how he's come into the postseason too small of a sample. And he's taken two walks.

So tomorrow is not gonna be the end-all, be-all because Sale is a tough match-up, but I still want to see good at-bats.

Q. With him, do you feel like it's more mental trying to do too much, or do you think that there might still be some adjustment coming back from the hand?

DAVE ROBERTS: I think there's trying to do too much. I think that clearly when he came back he was swinging the bat really well, had success and then I think there's a little bit of trying too much, yeah.

Looking at Dodgers CF Andy Pages in 2026

Pages is 0-for-7 with one walk and four strikeouts in the 2026 postseason.

He had a strong regular season, slashing .274/.343/.468 with 23 home runs and 85 RBI over 134 games.

The Dodgers placed Pages on the injured list on Aug. 22 with a left hand fracture.

Los Angeles reinstated Pages from the IL on Sept. 21. He finished the regular season strong, going 6-for-18 with two home runs, a double, four walks and five RBI over six games in September.

articles.title: Chris Olave tops the 100-yard mark once again
articles.summary: Chris Olave led all players with 12 targets, eight receptions, and 116 yards on Monday night against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints WR Chris Olave caught eight passes for 116 yards in a Week 4 loss to the Atlanta Falcons . Olave was targeted a game-high 12 times.

Why It Matters: For the third time in four games this season, Olave topped the century mark. The Ohio State product has developed into one of the most consistent performers at the position, and he has seen double-digit targets each week. The caveat with Olave continues to be red-zone production. He seemed to sort it out in 2025 with nine touchdowns, but in his other three seasons plus four weeks of 2026 he's scored just 11 times combined. While Olave is doing enough to offer WR1 value, until he starts finding the end zone more often he has to be considered to be a notch below the very top names at the position.

articles.title: Saints’ Kellen Moore is still trying to figure out solution to New Orleans’ slow starts
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints are running out of patience and answers. After Monday night’s humiliating 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons dropped New Orleans to 1-3...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints are running out of patience and answers. After Monday night's humiliating 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons dropped New Orleans to 1-3, head coach Kellen Moore admitted that his team's recurring slow starts remain an unresolved problem. It continues to put the Saints in difficult positions before their offense can find its rhythm.

"Yeah, it's just this point. Again, obviously not coaching it well enough, not executing it well enough," Moore said postgame. "They came out, went right down the field, scored, we went three and out. And we didn't score until the second quarter. We've tried a number of different things. And obviously we haven't solved this, but we gotta find a way."

Atlanta immediately exposed the problem Monday . The Falcons marched down the field for an opening touchdown before New Orleans answered with a three-and-out. Those early deficits have become particularly damaging with Travis Etienne Jr sidelined by injury. This has forced Tyler Shough and the passing game to shoulder more responsibility while the defense struggles to contain opposing rushing attacks.

New Orleans opened 2026 with a 31-30 loss to Detroit before beating Baltimore 24-17. Since then, losses to the Raiders and Falcons have exposed growing issues. Atlanta ran for more than 200 yards and scored five rushing touchdowns. That underscored the defensive concerns facing Moore's team.

The Saints now travel to Minnesota for Week 5 with little margin for error. Moore and his staff have tried multiple approaches to improve their opening sequences. However, the results remain unchanged. Until New Orleans finds a way to start games with urgency, its season could unravel before halftime becomes relevant.

articles.title: Commanders quarterback update: Latest on Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota
articles.summary: Commanders provide updates on Jayden Daniels' return and Marcus Mariota's injury.
articles.body:
After the Washington Commanders ' Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London, head coach Dan Quinn updated everyone on injured backup quarterback Marcus Mariota.

"The team thinks it's an MCL injury," Quinn said. "When we get the scan tomorrow, we'll have further knowledge of what we're dealing with and length and all those."

Mariota was injured on Washington's second drive in the first quarter after he was sacked and a defender landed on his leg. The injury looked scary and potentially season-ending. However, on Monday, Quinn provided more context on Mariota's injury, confirming it was a sprained MCL, the same injury he suffered in the first preseason game.

"Marcus sprained his MCL," Quinn said on Monday. "It's the same one that he injured in training camp. Don't have an exact timetable yet. We'll know a little bit more after his return-to-play process, but he'll be working off to the side as it goes through the next week or so."

That's terrific news for Mariota and the Commanders, considering it appeared much worse. Mariota missed around three weeks this summer with the same injury. Obviously, that doesn't mean this one follows on the exact same timeline, but barring setbacks, it should be close. Washington plays the New York Giants and San Francisco 49ers over the next two weeks before its Week 7 bye, which could line up Mariota for a Week 8 return.

As for starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, he'll return to practice on Wednesday, as expected, and take all the reps.

"Yeah, the goal is for him to have a full week of practice, full week, and start on Sunday," Quinn said.

No mystery there. Daniels will be in the lineup next week, three weeks after dislocating his left (non-throwing) elbow in Week 2 at Dallas. It's the same elbow that Daniels dislocated last November.

Daniels returning for Week 5 was already the plan. This isn't the Commanders panicking about possibly having to start rookie Athan Kaliakmanis against the Giants. Daniels was in London with the team last week, in his brace, to get some practice time before a full return this week.

It's certainly been a tough year for Washington on the injury front, especially at quarterback, but all things considered, the Commanders have been fortunate with Daniels and Mariota.

articles.title: Why Falcons’ Bijan Robinson loves showing out on primetime
articles.summary: The Falcons jumped out to a sizable early lead in New Orleans against the Saints before running away with a 45-24 road win that led to messages from star RB...
articles.body:
The Falcons jumped out to a sizable early lead in New Orleans against the Saints before running away with a 45-24 road win that led to messages from star RB Bijan Robinson and WR Drake London. A barrage of rushing touchdowns felled the home team as Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. staked their visiting team to victory at Caesars Superdome.

Afterward, Bijan Robinson revealed the biggest reason why he loves showing out in prime time games, and seems to have a knack for it.

"Well first off, I gotta give honor to God, without him, I wouldn't be here, we wouldn't be here, so I just gotta give thanks to him and all he's blessed me to do. I'm just doing it for this team, and I just gotta give thanks to Jesus, but yeah, prime time games are fun, I always tell the guys, and you wanna prove to your team that you wanna continue to be great in these moments, cause these are what bring us together.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"So, I love the prime time game under the lights, like, it just brings out a different energy, and I love it for the team."

Bijan Robinson led his team with 19 rushes for 145 yards and two touchdowns, dwarfing Saints counterpart Alvin Kamara's team-leading 23 yards and two touchdowns on the night. Bijan Robinson bested a Michael Turner franchise record with his first quarter assault on the Saints' defense, looking like a future First-Team All-Pro in the process.

October 11 will bring a matchup against the Ravens to the forefront of the Falcons' world as they will travel to Baltimore to face new head coach Jesse Minter's team. It's another prime time game, which could mean another big performance from Bijan Robinson, the former Texas Longhorns and current Falcons star.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards reveals surprising factor in LaMelo Ball’s Timberwolves debut
articles.summary: In limited action, LaMelo Ball showed how he can add another dynamic to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Ball helped the Timberwolves beat the Milwaukee Bucks, 1...
articles.body:
In limited action, LaMelo Ball showed how he can add another dynamic to the Minnesota Timberwolves . Ball helped the Timberwolves beat the Milwaukee Bucks , 116-97, in his preseason debut with his new squad.

Ball tallied 11 points, four rebounds, three assists, and one steal in 17 minutes. His chemistry with Anthony Edwards and Rudy Gobert was on point, a very encouraging sign for the Timberwolves.

Edwards had 14 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks in 18 minutes, while Gobert added six points and seven rebounds in 17 minutes.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Edwards gushed about Ball after the game, as reported by The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski.

"He was great tonight. Y'all know. He plays like his hair is on fire. He gets everybody involved. He talked more than I expected throughout the game. That's another big one for me, especially because I love people who talk. Let us know what you see," said the four-time All-Star.

Many are excited for the electric one-two punch of Edwards and Ball , who entered the NBA at the same time in 2020. Ball beat Edwards by a slim margin as Rookie of the Year.

They have publicly declared their mutual admiration for each other ahead of the new campaign, which should only improve their on-court connection. They have similar personalities as well, and that should make them a fun duo to watch.

Coach Chris Finch has repeatedly praised the 25-year-old Ball, who is coming off a strong season with the Charlotte Hornets.

"He brings a joy to the game. He's always fun to be around. He's got a fast chemistry with everybody, and I think we're getting him at the right time," said Finch, as quoted by Sports Illustrated's Andrew Carlson.

The Timberwolves will face the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday.

articles.title: 🗞️ The front pages: Messi bids farewell and Lamine Yamal's reign begins
articles.summary: Tuesday's front pages are all about celebrations: one is about to end, while the other has only just begun. Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal take centre stage....
articles.body:
Tuesday's front pages are all about celebrations: one is about to end, while the other has only just begun. Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal take centre stage.

Messi plays his final match for Argentina tonight (01:00) against Benin, and Olé turns it into a collective outpouring of tears with "Time to cry, my love".

Spain visit a Croatia side still hurting from their 7-0 defeat to England, and Marca , Sport and Mundo Deportivo are banking on Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí to lead the way into the quarter-finals.

Mundo Deportivo, meanwhile, leads today with Deco's efforts to tie down Barcelona's key players. Next in line for new contracts are Raphinha, Bernal and Espart.

The neighbouring national teams have already done their part: France turned a 1-0 deficit against Belgium into a 4-1 lead in fourteen minutes, with Olise scoring twice, while Italy dispatched Turkey 3-1 with goals from Scamacca, Calafiori and Pio Esposito.

In England, the Daily Star has Kane one appearance away from matching Peter Shilton's 125 caps, while Tuchel holds him up as a role model.

In Portugal, the action is also unfolding off the pitch. O Jogo reports that the relationship between Cristiano and Jorge Jesus has broken down.

And we finish with Estadio Deportivo and Superdeporte, featuring Ceballos, who would trade a Madrid trophy for one with Betis, and Gayà receiving tributes in Valencia.
